newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Philippines to pay oil firms dues in 1998.
newsitem.headline: Philippines to pay oil firms dues in 1998.

text.p: The Philippines said on Tuesday it is considering paying the 2.4 billion peso claims of the country's oil refiners through the 1998 budgetary allocation to be approved by Congress.

"...We have been instructed by President Ramos to assure the oil companies that their advances to make up for the OPSF deficiency will be reimbursed," Budget and Management minister Salvador Enriquez said in a statement.
The OPSF (Oil Price Stabilisation Fund) was a buffer fund created to reduce the impact of international oil price fluctuations on the local market.
Oil firms claimed money from it or paid into it depending on the difference between international and local prices.
With international prices outstripping the controlled local prices, the OPSF slipped into deficit.
Petron Corp has 1.085 billion pesos in claims from the fund while Pilipinas Shell Petroleum Corp, a unit of the Royal Dutch/Shell Group has 928.09 million in claims.
Caltex Philippines Inc, a unit of Caltex Petroleum Corp, a joint venture of Chevron Corp, is seeking 388.35 million pesos in reimbursements.

This year, the goverment approved a law deregulating the oil industry, which means prices would be freed from government control and the OPSF abolished. Full deregulation is scheduled for March next year.
